Is Understory a LinkedIn ghostwriting agency?

Understory or rallyup: which should I choose?

Choose Understory if you want LinkedIn content inside a wider SaaS growth program with paid ads and outbound from one team. Choose rallyup if you want executive content and audience building on its own, a published price per executive and a written guarantee of 100k organic impressions in 90 days, or we keep working for free until you get there (for B2B founders and executives with $5m+ in ARR or funding).
body:
the short answer

Understory Agency is a strong choice for a growth-stage or enterprise B2B SaaS company that wants LinkedIn content run inside a wider growth program, with paid media, Clay-built outbound and RevOps from the same team. If you only want executive LinkedIn content, or want a published price, the alternatives fit better. rallyup is the strongest fit for B2B founders and leadership teams who want a dedicated human writer per executive, a published price from $5,000 per executive per month and a guarantee of 100k organic impressions in 90 days, or we keep working for free until you get there. Windmill Growth suits a single founder who wants outbound and inbox management bundled in, and Kurogo suits UK executives who want carousels and graphics as standard.

rallyup publishes this page and is one of the alternatives listed. Every fact about Understory below comes from its own website, checked on November 24, 2026.

what understory offers

Understory describes itself as an "allbound B2B growth agency for SaaS": paid media, GTM engineering (signal-based outbound built in Clay), LinkedIn content and RevOps, run as one system. It lists No. 140 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 and says it is trusted by 150+ B2B companies.

Its LinkedIn content service is for founders and executive teams at growth-stage and enterprise B2B SaaS companies. As its page describes the process:

  • An intake form, a Slack channel and a Notion board at kickoff, plus a profile audit.
  • Research that scores 16 content styles by what lands with each buyer persona.
  • A voice interview every two weeks, led by your writer.
  • 16 or 30 posts a month, drafted about two weeks out in Ordinal, with text, carousels, infographics and your photos, and up to two rounds of revisions per post.
  • Winning posts run as thought-leader ads; ICP-fit engagers go into outreach as an add-on.

Its featured content result: Operatus, where a 90-minute interview each month with the CEO becomes 10 to 20 posts, most posts reach 5,000 to 10,000 impressions, the best reached 50,000, and engagement grew 600% in 90 days. Understory does not publish its prices; a call sets the scope.

who understory fits best

Understory fits a SaaS company that wants one partner for the whole demand engine: LinkedIn content plus paid ads, outbound and CRM work, with content amplified as ads. If you plan to buy several of those services anyway, keeping them under one team is a real advantage, and its content volume (16 or 30 posts a month) suits executives who want a high cadence.

why buyers compare alternatives

  • Content only. Teams that already run paid and outbound in-house often want executive content and audience building without a wider growth retainer.
  • A published price. Understory quotes per client. Some buyers want to compare a fixed, published price before a call.
  • Not SaaS. Understory's LinkedIn page is written for B2B SaaS. Fintech, VC and other B2B executives may want an agency with results in their space.
  • Volume. 16 to 30 posts a month is a lot of approvals for a busy executive. Some prefer fewer posts with more depth each.
  • A written result. Buyers who want a guarantee on reach, not only on output, compare agencies that put one in writing.

the alternatives

1. rallyup: best for founders and leadership teams who want content-led audience building

rallyup is a done-for-you LinkedIn and X ghostwriting agency for B2B founders and executives. Each executive gets a dedicated human writer, three posts a week published at peak times, a story interview twice a month and a profile rewrite, plus ICP connection requests and a monthly report. Every post is approved in Slack before it goes live. Pricing starts at $5,000 per executive per month, with a guarantee for B2B founders and executives with $5m+ in ARR or funding: 100k organic impressions in 90 days, or we keep working for free until you get there.

In our executive linkedin benchmarks 2026 (14 B2B executives), the 7 with complete account data grew monthly impressions a median 4.7x in the first 90 days, and 6 of those 7 at least doubled. Named results are on our case studies page, across SaaS (PandaDoc), fintech (Airwallex) and venture capital (Lightbank).

2. Windmill Growth: best for one founder who wants outbound too

Windmill Growth's Founder OS ($3,999 a month) covers a weekly 30-minute interview, up to 5 posts a week shared across LinkedIn and X, a profile rebuild, ICP outreach and inbox management for one founder. See our windmill growth alternatives page.

3. Kurogo: best for UK executives who want design

A London personal branding agency with 10 to 20 posts a month, carousels and graphics as standard, from £1,500 a month (light management) or £2,500 (full). See our kurogo alternatives page.

4. CSuite Content: best for CEOs who want PR too

Combines LinkedIn ghostwriting with op-eds, speeches and earned media. Pricing is quoted per client.

5. Sculpt: best for company-wide employee advocacy

Runs employee and executive social programs from $5,000 a month, with organic programs from $8,500. A fit when the goal is many employees posting, not a few executives.

6. A freelance ghostwriter: best for smaller budgets

One executive with time to brief and manage a writer can spend less. See ghostwriter vs agency.

how to choose

  • Are you buying content, or a growth engine? If you also want paid ads, outbound and CRM work, an allbound team like Understory makes sense. If you want executive content and audience building, pay for that alone.
  • How many executives will post? Compare per-executive pricing with team retainers.
  • How much review can the executive do? Thirty posts a month means thirty approvals.
  • What will you measure? Ask each agency for a sample monthly report and for results from a company like yours.

when rallyup isn't the right fit

  • You want paid ads, outbound and RevOps from the same agency as your content. An allbound team fits better.
  • Your budget is under $5,000 a month per executive. A freelance ghostwriter is the better choice.
  • You want 20 or more posts a month per executive.
  • The executive can't give a 30-minute story interview twice a month.
